To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mass of the vector boson lifts the degeneracies between the transverse modes in D=4 and excites the s-wave of the longitudinal mode in D>4.

the transmission factors of the Proca field are different than the scalar transmission factor and that the longitudinal modes of the Proca are excited by the mass term, in particular the mass term excites the s-wave mode of the longitudinal mode.

Hawking radiation for a massive vector bosons can be obtained by solving the coupled wave equations for all physical modes, and that it can be computed from the transmission factors of decoupled modes, as done previously for a massless field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the Hawking radiation of a massive vector field in D-dimension.
the Hawking radiation of a massive Proca field in Schwarzschild space-time.
a new way to compute Hawking radiation for a massive vector field, which can be extended to any massive spin field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Proca field in the black hole background is not a simple scalar field, but a more complex one, and that its Hawking radiation is not the same as that of a scalar field.
the Hawking flux of a Proca field is larger than for the scalar case, and the mass term introduces an energy scale which determines the transition from scalar-like to vector-like behaviour.
, for the case of a massive vector field, the longitudinal mode does not decouple and the Hawking emission rate depends strongly on the mass of the field and the dimension of the spacetime.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mass term of the Proca field is a crucial ingredient for a correct description of the Hawking flux in this channel, and the longitudinal mode must be included.
the Hawking radiation for a massive vector field in the background of Schwarzschild black holes is significantly different from that of a scalar field, even at the level of the transmission factors.
the Hawking flux of a massive vector field is not a simple superposition of the fluxes of a scalar field with the same mass and a massless vector field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the presence of a mass term, the Hawking flux is dominated by the longitudinal mode at intermediate energies.
the mass term of the Proca field can be important for black hole production in TeV gravity models, and that it should be taken into account for a correct modelling of the Hawking radiation.
the Hawking emission in the Proca channel can be comparable to the one in the scalar case, and it should be taken into account in phenomenological studies.
